prerequisites: Basic knowledge on C/C++ and Python programming
basic skills on using virtualization technologies

learning_outcomes.text: The graduate has adequate knowledge of the protocols by which the Internet works and has the necessary skills to design and test his/her own protocols.
The graduate has the basic knowledge required to install, configure and maintain a server system on the Internet.
The graduate possesses the basic knowledge of operating system specific programming and is familiar with scripting languages.
The graduate is able to design and maintain a computer network of medium complexity.
The graduate is able to present and explain methods, algorithms, paradigms and techniques used in various branches of computer science.
The graduate has the ability to observe and obtain information from various sources.
The graduate has the ability to understand and communicate information effectively.

syllabus_topics: Computer Networks Introduction. Definition. Examples. Network Topologies.
The socket programming API. Network programming using TCP and UDP.
Protocols: definition. Protocol layers. The OSI reference model. The TCP/IP layered model.
The functions and services of the IP layer. Structure of an IP datagram. IP addressing (classfull). Datagram check summing. The ARP protocol.
The concept of Subnetworks and Supernetworks. CIDR. Network masks.
The UDP protocol and services. The structure of an UDP datagram UDP ports and processes.
The TCP protocol. Structure of a TCP segment. Principles of TCP data transmission.
The TCP Sliding Window mechanism. Flow Control. Congestion avoidance.
Broadcast and multicast communication. The ICMP protocol. Error and network state signaling.
The application layer. HTTP, SMTP, FTP
The Internet Domain Name System. The DNS protocol.
Network routing. Distance based and link state based routing algorithms. Routing protocols: RIP, BGP, OSPF.
The physical layer. Transmission media. Characteristics, fiber networks, wireless networks. Error detection and correction.
Network Security; Netiquette and computer network behavior norms.
Laboratory Configuration. Necessary tools, Virtual machines and build systems;
A simple client-server TCP application;
Concurrent TCP client-server applications;
Concurrent Multiplexed TCP- Servers. The select call. Network debugging – wireshark
Simple UDP client-server; Security Handling;
Complex/Concurrent UDP applications. Ping. Traceroute. Ipconfig/ifconfig.
TCP/IP programming -Mid term evaluation;
Packet Tracer - simple network simulation
Packet Tracer - Physical/logical network design
Packet Tracer - Static Routing, NAT
Packet Tracer – RIP Routing
Packet Tracer – Packet filtering and VLANs
Packet Tracer – Complex design
Lab Evaluation.

assessment_methods.method: Mid-term and final term lab tests or overall lab grade

assessment_rules: At least a grading of 5 (from a scale of 1 to 10) is required at both the theoretical exam and laboratory assessments.
